findings.title: configSchema is a ZodEffects (ends in .superRefine); 'add fields to configSchema' is not mechanically possible as written
findings.location: design.md §1 'New variables added to configSchema' and 'Cross-field superRefine guards'
findings.problem: src/config/env.ts exports configSchema as z.object({...}).superRefine(...), i.e. a ZodEffects, not a ZodObject. New fields must go inside the .object({...}) literal before .superRefine, and new cross-field guards inside the body of the single existing superRefine callback. The design's loose 'added alongside' phrasing invites configSchema.extend(...) or a second chained .superRefine, neither of which works correctly on a ZodEffects.
findings.fix: State explicitly: new fields are inserted into the existing z.object({...}) literal before the trailing .superRefine; new MODE cross-field guards are added as ctx.addIssue blocks inside the existing single superRefine callback after the auth/email guards; AppConfig stays z.infer<typeof configSchema>; no .extend() and no second .superRefine().

findings.title: Agent-mode boot order for createPm2Adapter is unspecified; the standalone 'bind-then-wire-PM2-in-background' guarantee does not carry over and AC-14 can be violated
findings.location: design.md §3 'constructed exactly as in standalone'; §8 item 8 (src/boot/agent.ts)
findings.problem: createPm2Adapter (src/pm2/client.ts) neutralizes inherited IPC and gates connect on a local pingDaemon, attaching only to an already-running daemon. In standalone, index.ts builds it in a background task AFTER server.listen so a hung/absent daemon never blocks boot. The agent binds no HTTP server, so that anchor is gone; the design never says the agent preserves the same 'never block the outbound WS dial on local PM2 connect' deferral, nor how a control:request arriving before PM2 attaches is answered. A synchronous adapter build before dialing can violate AC-14 (keep the server connection while local PM2 is down).
findings.fix: Specify bootstrapAgent() starts the AgentConnection dial loop first/concurrently and wires createPm2Adapter/Pm2Client.start() in a background task exactly as index.ts, using the same PM2_UNAVAILABLE/[] facade until the real client is wired, so a control:request before PM2 attaches returns a correlated PM2_UNAVAILABLE ControlResult and the dial is never blocked by local PM2.

findings.title: logger.ts docstring ('shallow + one level nested') is stale vs. the full-depth recursion the design now relies on
findings.problem: The design's corrected depth analysis is accurate against the code, but the logger.ts module docstring still says '(shallow + one level nested)', contradicting the real behavior the design depends on. An implementer reading the stale doc may weaken the redaction test to match it.
findings.fix: Add a line to §7 noting the logger.ts docstring is stale (implementation recurses to full depth), that the §9 redaction-depth test is the source of truth, and to update the docstring while adding the keys.

findings.title: Agent start-new sanitization uses ALLOWED_SCRIPT_ROOT but §1 never lists/threads it for agent mode
findings.problem: ALLOWED_SCRIPT_ROOT already exists (all modes) but the agent config list omits it and the design never states the agent threads config.ALLOWED_SCRIPT_ROOT into buildSchemas, leaving it ambiguous whether an operator can confine remote start-new per agent host.
findings.fix: Add a one-line wiring note: the agent builds RequestSchemas via buildSchemas({ allowedScriptRoot: config.ALLOWED_SCRIPT_ROOT }), reusing the existing variable so remote start-new can be confined per host as in standalone.

findings.title: Routed-create HTTP status: 201 must apply only to the ok branch; not-ok create must use statusForControlCode
findings.problem: Standalone create returns 201 on success (sendControlResult(res,result,201)). statusForControlCode maps only failures; success is described as '200 (or 201 for create)'. A routed create can also fail (VALIDATION->400, AGENT_OFFLINE->409). The design should pin that 201 applies only when result.ok, else statusForControlCode governs, so an implementer does not hardcode 201 for the create route regardless of ok-ness.
findings.fix: Pin in §4: agents create route returns 201 only when result.ok===true; a not-ok create result uses statusForControlCode(result.code) with the error envelope, identical to other control endpoints; non-create control returns 200 on ok.

findings.title: register:nack and handshake-timeout close paths are not stated to share the idempotent onLinkDead guard
findings.location: design.md §3 'Connection + reconnect' and 'Heartbeat and single-path liveness'
findings.problem: The two liveness paths funnel through an idempotent onLinkDead(), but register:nack's 'close + schedule reconnect' and the transport close from the server's 5s handshake timeout are additional teardown triggers whose relationship to onLinkDead() is unstated. If separate, a single event could schedule two reconnects — the exact double-trigger onLinkDead was designed to prevent.
findings.fix: State that all socket-teardown paths (register:nack, handshake-timeout/transport close, heartbeat/pong dead-link) funnel through the single idempotent onLinkDead() so exactly one reconnect is scheduled; register:nack additionally logs the nack code before calling it.
